name: Accounting and ERP
description: Invoicing, bookkeeping and connected business operations.
audience: Business owners, finance teams and bookkeepers across industries
audienceRationale: Financial record keeping spans business sizes and sectors; finance users operate software directly.

name: API clients and testing
description: Develop, inspect and automate tests for HTTP and other APIs, with explicit separation between local clients and managed team platforms.
audience: Software developers, API QA engineers and technical integration teams
audienceRationale: Daily utility for API development and quality assurance roles; narrower than general business collaboration tools.

name: Workflow automation
description: Connect business apps and automate multi-step processes with triggers, actions and orchestration.
audience: Business operations, sales, marketing, IT and other teams connecting everyday applications.
audienceRationale: Cross-department workflow integration; relevant across industries, but requires processes that benefit from automation.

name: Backup and recovery
description: Create recoverable file backups and restore lost data; distinguish managed endpoint services from self-operated backup tools and full-system disaster recovery.
audience: Individuals protecting computer files and IT teams operating endpoint or server backups.
audienceRationale: File loss and device failure affect personal and business computing; operation of server repositories requires technical administration.

name: Business intelligence
description: Database exploration, metrics, dashboards and scheduled analytical reporting.
audience: Business analysts, data teams, managers and operational teams consuming business metrics.
audienceRationale: Reporting supports many business functions; configuration and semantic modeling are concentrated in analysts and data teams.

name: CRM
description: Manage contacts, sales opportunities, pipelines, and customer relationships.
audience: Sales teams, account managers, founders, and customer-facing staff across industries.
audienceRationale: Cross-industry sales and customer operations, from small businesses to enterprise teams; less universal than email or file storage.

name: Diagramming
description: Create flowcharts, process maps, technical diagrams and visual documentation.
audience: Business teams, educators, engineers and developers communicating processes and systems.
audienceRationale: Process and system diagrams span business, technical and education work; creation is an occasional or specialist task for many users.

name: Digital Asset Management
description: Catalog, search, govern and share photos, video, brand files and other media with structured metadata and access controls.
audience: Marketing and creative teams, brand managers, media librarians, archives and cultural institutions.
audienceRationale: A recurring function across industries, primarily used by teams managing reusable media collections rather than every employee.

name: Docs and wiki
description: Team documentation, internal wikis and shared knowledge workspaces.
audience: Employees and teams documenting decisions, procedures, project plans and institutional knowledge.
audienceRationale: Documentation spans business functions; adoption does not require a specialist department. Qualitative potential reach, not a headcount estimate.

name: Document Management
description: Capture, OCR, organize, search and control business documents, with document workflows and access permissions.
audience: Operations, finance, HR, records administrators and teams managing document collections.
audienceRationale: Document capture and retrieval span business departments and industries; advanced approval and governance needs vary by organization.

name: E-signature
description: Send business documents for electronic signature and track completion.
audience: Businesses sending contracts, offers, purchase agreements, waivers, and approvals.
audienceRationale: Agreement workflows span sales, HR, procurement, operations, and customer onboarding; use varies with document volume.

name: Ecommerce
description: Build online storefronts and manage catalogs, checkout, orders and commerce integrations.
audience: Online merchants and the developers or agencies building their stores.
audienceRationale: Used across industries by businesses selling online; adoption centers on commerce operations and implementation teams.

name: Email clients and webmail
description: Desktop email clients and browser webmail for individual mailbox workflows.
audience: Individuals and organizations reading, organizing, and sending email across existing mail accounts.
audienceRationale: Personal and work email spans occupations and organization sizes; desktop and browser access serve general mailbox needs. Shared customer-support operations are a separate capability.

name: Business email hosting
description: Custom-domain mailbox servers and groupware; distinguishes email hosting from complete office suites and mail clients.
audience: Organizations operating custom-domain employee email, and IT administrators responsible for delivery and mailbox infrastructure.
audienceRationale: Custom-domain email serves businesses across functions; self-operated server selection and ongoing delivery operations chiefly concern IT teams. Qualitative audience reach, not a counted market estimate.

name: Email marketing
description: Newsletters, subscriber segmentation, campaigns and marketing automation.
audience: Businesses, charities and publishers communicating with prospects and customers.
audienceRationale: Customer communication spans industries and organization sizes, although primarily used by marketing and business owners.

name: Expense reimbursements
description: Employee expense claims, receipt submission, approval workflows and reimbursement status.
audience: Employees claiming business expenses, approving managers and finance operations teams.
audienceRationale: Expense reimbursement spans employers across industries; employees submit claims while managers and finance teams approve and settle them.

name: File transfer
description: Send, receive and share large files through browser links or client delivery portals.
audience: Individuals, client-facing teams, creative studios and organizations exchanging files externally.
audienceRationale: File delivery spans individual sharing and recurring client work across industries; specialized high-volume routing serves production teams.

name: Forms and surveys
description: Collect leads, feedback, questionnaires, polls and research responses.
audience: Marketing, customer success, HR, operations, product and research teams across business sizes.
audienceRationale: Forms and feedback span multiple business functions and industries; adoption is broad but not required by every employee.

name: Application hosting and backends
description: Deployment platforms and backend services for business web and mobile applications.
audience: Software teams and businesses building their own applications
audienceRationale: Relevant across industries but directly used by software delivery teams rather than every employee.

name: Human resources
description: Employee records, leave, recruiting, onboarding, attendance, performance and payroll administration.
audience: Employers, HR teams, managers and employee self-service users.
audienceRationale: Employee administration spans industries and company sizes; HR staff manage the system while employees use leave and attendance workflows.

name: Image editing
description: Raster image retouching, compositing and digital painting, plus RAW photo development and library workflows.
audience: Photographers, designers, illustrators and people preparing images for work or personal projects.
audienceRationale: Image preparation spans creative professions and occasional general use; RAW development and digital painting are more specialized workflows within the category.

name: Internal tools and low-code apps
description: Build admin panels, operational apps and workflows over databases and APIs.
audience: Operations and IT teams, developers and business teams building bespoke internal software
audienceRationale: Cross-industry use, but direct buyers are teams creating custom internal software rather than every employee.

name: IT asset management
description: Hardware/software asset inventory, ownership and lifecycle records; discovery and service-management capabilities differ.
audience: IT, procurement and operations teams managing organization devices and software inventory.
audienceRationale: Assets affect most staff, but the direct operators and buyers are IT and procurement specialists rather than all employees.

name: Kanban
description: Visual boards for team tasks and workflow stages.
audience: Teams across business functions managing shared tasks.
audienceRationale: Trello explicitly targets marketing, product, engineering, design, startups and remote teams; useful across functions without requiring a specialist role.

name: Learning management
description: Create and deliver courses, enroll learners, assess progress and manage organizational training.
audience: Education providers, trainers and learning and development teams.
audienceRationale: Specialized administrators and educators operate systems serving learners across schools and organizations.

name: Login and single sign-on
description: Workforce SSO, application/customer identity and web access authentication; distinct use cases with partial overlap.
audience: IT/security teams managing employee application access and software teams implementing customer login.
audienceRationale: Employee access spans industries; customer IAM also serves businesses operating applications. Deployment requires identity and security expertise.

name: Monitoring and observability
description: Infrastructure dashboards, website uptime, and application error tracking; mappings scoped by capability.
audience: Engineering, IT operations, site reliability and website owners
audienceRationale: Relevant to organizations operating software or websites; specialized users manage it even where business impact is broad.

name: Office suite and files
description: Business document editing, office collaboration and file sync/share; distinguish integrated hubs from file platforms and editor components.
audience: Business teams across functions creating, storing and collaborating on documents.
audienceRationale: Documents, spreadsheets and shared files recur across most office-based businesses; broad suite and storage incumbents address small teams through enterprises. This is qualitative reach, not a measured market-size ranking.

name: Password managers
description: Store, share and administer business credentials.
audience: Employees and organizations using online accounts
audienceRationale: Credentials and controlled sharing apply across industries and company sizes; qualitative reach, not a market-size estimate.

name: PDF editing and processing
description: Tools to edit PDF content or organize, split, merge, convert and process PDF documents.
audience: People handling forms, reports, scans and other PDF documents at home, school and work.
audienceRationale: PDF work spans many roles and personal document tasks; editing and page processing are distinct needs.

name: Project management
description: Plan projects, track work and coordinate delivery across teams.
audience: Business teams, project managers and product/development teams
audienceRationale: Cross-functional work coordination spans operations, marketing, services and technical teams; specialist agile use cases are a subset.

name: Recruiting and applicant tracking
description: Job openings, candidate applications, hiring pipelines, interviews, feedback and offers.
audience: Recruiters, talent acquisition teams, staffing agencies and hiring managers.
audienceRationale: Hiring spans industries, while daily ATS operation centers on recruiting specialists and hiring managers rather than all employees.

name: Appointment scheduling
description: Booking links, availability, appointments and service-provider scheduling.
audience: Sales, recruiting, customer-facing teams and service businesses.
audienceRationale: Cross-industry need for customer and colleague bookings, especially customer-facing teams; less universal than office communication.

name: Screen recording and asynchronous video
description: Record demonstrations, tutorials, feedback and asynchronous team video.
audience: Knowledge workers, support, sales, product and training teams
audienceRationale: Cross-functional business communication and demonstrations, with adoption dependent on video workflows.

name: Search infrastructure
description: Search engines and APIs for application search, indexing and selected search analytics workloads.
audience: Product and platform engineering teams
audienceRationale: Engineers maintaining search-backed applications; end users benefit indirectly, but most business employees do not procure or operate search infrastructure.

name: Social publishing
description: Plan, schedule and publish social media content across accounts.
audience: Creators, marketers, agencies and communications teams
audienceRationale: Publishing spans many sectors but serves a specific marketing/communications function.

name: Spreadsheet databases
description: Relational business data with spreadsheet editing, forms and configurable views.
audience: Operations, marketing, sales, HR, finance and project teams building shared business trackers and lightweight internal apps.
audienceRationale: Cross-functional business records and workflows apply across many industries; requires structured-data collaboration rather than every employee role.

name: Support and helpdesk
description: Customer support ticketing, shared inboxes, chat and self-service.
audience: Businesses handling customer questions and service requests; dedicated support teams.
audienceRationale: Support crosses retail, software and services and spans small businesses through enterprises; dedicated tooling becomes relevant once shared inbox workflows become insufficient.

name: Team chat
description: Persistent team messaging, channels, direct messages, and collaborative conversations.
audience: Employees and external collaborators across business functions and industries.
audienceRationale: A cross-functional communication need shared by distributed and office-based teams; reach ranking is qualitative, not a headcount estimate.

name: Telephony
description: Business voice calling, PBX and call-center telephony, including self-operated communications engines.
audience: Business phone users, sales and support teams, telephony administrators and communications developers.
audienceRationale: Business calling spans many departments and industries; operating the OSS engines requires specialist communications skills.

name: Time tracking
description: Track work hours by client and project, analyze timesheets, and prepare billable work.
audience: Freelancers, agencies, consultants, and teams recording project or billable hours.
audienceRationale: Relevant across professional services and project-driven teams; recording work hours is a recurring need across industries.

name: Transcription & Meeting Notes
description: Turn recorded or live speech into text; meeting services add capture, summaries and collaboration, while open engines provide a lower-level alternative.
audience: People documenting meetings, interviews and recordings; developers building private speech-to-text workflows.
audienceRationale: Speech-to-text supports recurring meetings and recorded content across roles; engine deployment requires technical integration.

name: Video calls
description: Browser and app video meetings, screen sharing, and virtual classrooms.
audience: Businesses holding internal meetings, customer calls, and remote training.
audienceRationale: Meeting tools serve staff across functions and industries; classroom software is a narrower training use case.

name: Video editing
description: Non-linear desktop video editing, audio mixing, titles, effects, grading and rendered output.
audience: Video creators, filmmakers, editors and marketing teams.
audienceRationale: Used across industries by people creating edited video; the workflow requires creative production skills rather than serving every employee.

name: VPN and private network access
description: Identity-aware private connectivity for remote staff, devices and internal resources.
audience: IT and security teams serving remote staff
audienceRationale: Many employees benefit from private access, while product selection and operation primarily belong to network, IT and security teams; narrower buying audience than general business collaboration.

name: Web analytics
description: Website traffic, acquisition, conversion and visitor behavior measurement.
audience: Website owners and marketing, product and growth teams across industries.
audienceRationale: Relevant to organizations with websites or digital products; specialist staff often operate the tools.

name: Websites and CMS
description: Build websites and manage published content.
audience: Individuals, small businesses, publishers, agencies and organizations maintaining websites.
audienceRationale: Website publishing serves personal, commercial, nonprofit and institutional needs across industries.

name: Whiteboards and UI design
description: Collaborative visual thinking, sketching and interface design; whiteboard and UI-design mappings are distinct.
audience: Cross-functional workshop participants, product teams, designers and engineers.
audienceRationale: Whiteboarding spans operations, marketing and product collaboration; professional interface design has a narrower designer/developer audience.
